messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Bug in generated transform_inits
parts:
There seems to be a bug in the transform_inits generated by gm.  Specifically, all the parameter initializations are written into a stan::io::writer class, but the values are never copied back into the params_i__ and params_r__ objects.  The net result is that user specified initializations are completely ignored.  I'm not sure the best way to fix this.

The solution I found is to add the lines

        params_r__.swap(writer__.data_r());
        params_i__.swap(writer__.data_i());

to the end of the generated transform_inits function.

This turn up a bug in the stan::io::writer class.  Specifically, by declaration the functions data_r() and data_() are supposed to return references but instead were returning pointers.  The following is a corrected version of the code

      std::vector<T>& data_r() {
        return data_r_;
      }

      std::vector<int>& data_i() {
        return data_i_;
      }


These are pretty small changes, but if people would like I can send along a diff.

With these changes I was able to use a hand specified initialization.

Cheers,
Marcus

This is why I love open source. Thanks so much
for not only reporting the bug but fixing it.

I'm going to push a patch, but I'm in the middle of
adding matrix operators, so I'll stage it after that.

Specific comments inline.

On 3/5/12 2:11 PM, Marcus Brubaker wrote:
> There seems to be a bug in the transform_inits generated by gm.
> Specifically, all the parameter initializations are written into a
> stan::io::writer class, but the values are never copied back into the
> params_i__ and params_r__ objects. The net result is that user
> specified initializations are completely ignored. I'm not sure the best
> way to fix this.
>
> The solution I found is to add the lines
> params_r__.swap(writer__.data_r());
> params_i__.swap(writer__.data_i());
>
> to the end of the generated transform_inits function.

I'll just do an assign rather than a swap just in
case anyone on the outside is relying on the params_r__
ref not changing. This won't happen very often (once
per chain), so the performance diff shouldn't be measurable.

> This turn up a bug in the stan::io::writer class. Specifically, by
> declaration the functions data_r() and data_() are supposed to return
> references but instead were returning pointers. The following is a
> corrected version of the code
>
> std::vector<T>& data_r() {
> return data_r_;
> }
>
> std::vector<int>& data_i() {
> return data_i_;
> }

Thanks. That's just my underlying ignorance of C++
showing through. I keep forgetting that it will figure
out refs vs. values for you in return and argument contexts.
This still somehow seems wrong to me.

> These are pretty small changes, but if people would like I can send
> along a diff.

> With these changes I was able to use a hand specified initialization.
>
> Cheers,
> Marcus

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Bug in generated transform_inits
parts:
On Mon, Mar 5, 2012 at 2:54 PM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:
This is why I love open source.  Thanks so much
for not only reporting the bug but fixing it.

No problem, I'm glad I can help.  Hopefully I can make some more substantial contributions as I get more familiar with the code base.

I realized that I forgot one last change that was necessary to get initializations working properly.  In command.hpp, the sampler needs to have its state set before being sampled from.  I.E., before the sample_from() calls around line 410/420 there should also be a call:

nuts_sampler.set_params(params_r,params_i);

or

hmc_sampler.set_params(params_r,params_i);

as appropriate.

Cheers,
Marcus
